properties.title: Flood Warning issued November 20 at 5:21AM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.The St Johns River at Astor is forecast to continue to rise through
Moderate Flood Stage, reaching Major Flood Stage early next week due
to heavy rainfall working its way through the basin in combination
with strong north-northeast flow.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and major flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 4.0 feet, Major flooding occurs with water entering
many structures on canals and along the river. Long duration
flooding will occur, with levels taking weeks to months to return
below flood stage. Water rescues will be necessary. River Road
becomes inaccessible, with 1 to 2 feet water depth in numerous
homes on Wildhog, Possum, Bonnet and Snail roads. Roads along Blue
Creek are inaccessible with major flooding of homes on Otter,
Branch and Chestnut roads. Camp South Moon Road and Juno Trail are
inaccessible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 4:30 AM EST Friday the stage was 3.6 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 4:30 AM EST Friday was 3.6 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to 4.0 feet Tuesday
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this morning at 1100 AM EST.

properties.title: Flood Warning issued November 20 at 3:10AM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Cocoa 9w affecting Brevard County.

.Extreme rainfall over the headwaters of the St. Johns River has
caused the river near Cocoa to rise through Major Flood Stage, well
above its previous record flood stage. Any additional heavy rainfall
over the next 48 hours will continue to produce river rises above
record flood levels through late week and into this weekend.

For the St. Johns River...including Cocoa 9w...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.
This approaches the flood of record.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Cocoa 9w.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 17.2 feet, Water enters homes along the St Johns River
in the Lake Poinsett area west of Cocoa, also low lying homes in
the Silver Pines subdivision in Rockledge and the Shakespeare Park
area of Cocoa. Providence Road area west of Cocoa becomes
impassable, cutting off access to homes in the Mullet Lane and Bass
Road area. Docks flooded and water in parking lot at Lone Cabbage
Fish Camp.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 2:15 AM EST Friday the stage was 18.6 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 15.8 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 2:15 AM EST Friday was 18.6 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain steady within Major
Flood Stage, cresting at 18.7 feet.
- Flood stage is 16.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

To escape rising water, take the shortest path to higher ground.

properties.title: Flash Flood Warning issued November 20 at 2:58AM EST until November 20 at 6:00AM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
FFWMLB

The National Weather Service in Melbourne has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Central Brevard County in east central Florida...

* Until 600 AM EST.

* At 258 AM EST, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain across the warned
area. Up to 1.5 and 2.5 inches of rain have fallen over the past
few hours, on top of areas that have already received very heavy
rainfall over the past 24 hours. Additional rainfall amounts of 1
to 2 inches are possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is
ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by heavy rain.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Titusville, Rockledge, Cocoa, Cocoa Beach, Satellite Beach, Cape
Canaveral, Sharpes, Port Saint John, Port Canaveral, Merritt
Island, Titusville Airport, Patrick Space Force Base, Jetty Park,
Canaveral Groves, Viera, South Patrick Shores, Palm Shores,
Bellwood and Canaveral Acres.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

properties.title: Flood Warning issued November 19 at 11:40PM EST until November 20 at 7:55PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

Little Wekiva River near Altamonte Springs 2n affecting Seminole
County.

.The Little Wekiva River near Altamonte Springs continues to
gradually rise as rainfall works through the basin. Additional heavy
rainfall with amounts of 2 to 4 inches will be possible through
tomorrow, which could lead to additional rises. The river is forecast
to reach Minor Flood Stage Friday morning and will continue in flood
stage through Friday evening.

For the Little Wekiva...including Altamonte Springs 2n...Minor
flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Little Wekiva River near Altamonte Springs 2n.

* WHEN...From Friday morning to Friday evening.

* IMPACTS...At 28.5 feet, Minor flooding near the river in the
Altamonte Springs area.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 10:30 PM EST Thursday the stage was 27.1 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 27.5 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage Friday
morning, cresting at 28.7 feet late Friday morning into Friday
afternoon. It will then fall below flood stage tomorrow evening.
Additional rises due to heavy rainfall cannot be ruled out.
- Flood stage is 28.5 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by upstream dam release continues.

* WHERE...Maricopa County in south central Arizona...
Northeastern Yuma County in southwestern Arizona...

* WHEN...Until 1100 AM MST Tuesday Nov 24.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is expected. Low-water crossings are
likely to become inundated with water and may not be passable.
